articles.title: Acidentes de trabalho em Juiz de Fora: mortes superam taxa de BH | G1
articles.standfirst: Cidade registra 18 mortes relacionadas ao trabalho em 2026, segundo a Secretaria de Estado de Saúde. Procurador do MPT aponta concentração de atividades de maior risco de acidentes.
articles.summary: Acidentes de trabalho em Juiz de Fora somam 18 mortes em 2026, com taxa de óbitos superior à de BH.
articles.body:
Construção civil segue entre os setores mais críticos, segundo promotor — Foto: Reprodução/TV Integração

Juiz de Fora é a segunda cidade de Minas Gerais com mais mortes por acidentes de trabalho em 2026 , apesar de ser a quarta mais populosa do estado. Dados da Secretaria de Estado de Saúde apontam que, até outubro, 18 trabalhadores morreram em ocorrências relacionadas ao trabalho no município, número inferior somente ao de Belo Horizonte, que registrou 24 óbitos .

Quando o número de habitantes é levado em consideração, a diferença chama ainda mais atenção. Enquanto Belo Horizonte registra uma taxa de 1,04 morte por acidente de trabalho a cada 100 mil habitantes, em Juiz de Fora o índice chega a 3,33 óbitos por 100 mil habitantes, mais de três vezes maior que o da capital .

Em entrevista ao g1 , o procurador do Ministério Público do Trabalho de Juiz de Fora, Fabricio Borela Pena, disse que esse destaque se deve ao fato de o município concentrar atividades econômicas que, normalmente, possuem mais registros de acidentes .

"A gente tem um setor de serviços forte, um setor de saúde expressivo, além de transporte, logística e construção civil. Quanto maior é a exposição de trabalhadores a essas atividades de maior risco, aumenta também a necessidade de prevenção”, destacou.

De acordo com Fabrício, a construção civil segue entre os setores mais críticos por envolver riscos como quedas de altura, soterramentos e choques elétricos. Transporte, logística e indústria também registram ocorrências frequentes devido à movimentação de cargas e à operação de máquinas pesadas. Na área da saúde , os principais riscos estão relacionados à exposição biológica e ao contato com materiais perfurocortantes.

Essa realidade se reflete nos números. Além dos óbitos, no mesmo período, foram registradas 1.058 notificações de acidentes de trabalho em Juiz de Fora. Entre os trabalhadores acidentados, a ocupação com maior número de registros foi a de faxineiro (10,81%), seguida pela de pedreiro (7,34%), servente de obras (4,25%), repositor de mercadorias (4,21%) e vendedor do comércio varejista (3,51%) .

Diante do elevado número de ocorrências registradas nessas atividades, é necessário um maior cuidado na prevenção desses acidentes. Segundo Fabrício, a cultura de prevenção nas empresas é um dos principais fatores para evitar que essas ocorrências aconteçam.

"É fundamental a capacitação, o treinamento e a orientação dos trabalhadores. É preciso haver uma cultura de prevenção, com ações desenvolvidas ao longo do tempo, de forma consistente, e não apenas um treinamento inicial", afirmou.

Apesar do número expressivo, ele destaca que a subnotificação é uma variável importante e precisa ser considerada. Segundo o procurador, os dados oficiais contemplam apenas os casos registrados pelos sistemas de notificação, o que pode esconder a real dimensão do problema.

“Infelizmente, se esses dados já são alarmantes, a gente tem que concluir que eles são apenas uma fração da realidade. Existe uma grande subnotificação no trabalho. A saúde mental é muito subnotificada, muitas vezes não é identificada como um problema decorrente do trabalho e isso não vai para os registros públicos.”

O procurador orienta que trabalhadores que identificarem situações de risco podem e devem denunciar o caso ao Ministério Público do Trabalho através do site . As denúncias são anônimas.

"Quando há risco grave e iminente, o Ministério Público e o Ministério do Trabalho atuam em caráter de urgência, com fiscalização e até interdição do estabelecimento, para garantir a segurança dos trabalhadores."

articles.title: 3 women dead, 3 others critically injured in North Hollywood Metro Station crash
articles.summary: Three women were killed and two pedestrians and were critically injured Tuesday evening when an SUV careened onto a sidewalk and struck a group of street ven...
articles.body:
Three women were killed and two pedestrians and were critically injured Tuesday evening when an SUV careened onto a sidewalk and struck a group of street vendors and commuters near the North Hollywood Metro Station, authorities said.

The collision was reported at approximately 5:55 p.m. on Nov. 10 in the 5300 block of North Lankershim Boulevard, near Chandler Boulevard, according to the Los Angeles Fire Department .

The three victims were pronounced dead at the scene, while paramedics transported two additional victims to local hospitals in critical condition.

"I saw all the bodies on the ground," one man who witnessed the tragic crash told KTLA. "I take the Metro every day and you see these vendors here. They're just working. I don't usually purchase anything from them, but I have a face-to-face nod, like, 'Hey, how's it going' with them."

Los Angeles police said the driver, a man in his early 60s, was traveling southbound on Lankershim Boulevard when his light-colored SUV struck at least five pedestrians near a busy public transit hub.

Aerial footage of the scene captured by KTLA's Sky5 showed the vehicle had come to rest on the sidewalk, beneath the canopy of a food vendor's tent.

Debris was scattered across the sidewalk and the heavily traveled Lankershim Boulevard corridor, where commuters regularly board buses and trains.

Sky5 also captured the driver, who had to be extricated from the vehicle. He appeared to be conscious and speaking with firefighters as emergency personnel helped him into a wheelchair and into the back of a waiting ambulance, though, according to KTLA Reporter Mary Beth McDade, his injuries were not life threatening.

Investigators have not determined what caused the crash, and police have not ruled out the possibility that it was intentional.

"We don't know if it was done intentionally, if it was done by accident," LAPD Capt. Warner Castillo said during a Tuesday night news conference, according to the Associated Press .

Castillo said investigators were examining whether the driver was impaired. Authorities have not established that drugs or alcohol played a role in the collision.

LAPD Chief Jim McDonnell said detectives would review surveillance footage from nearby businesses and the Metro station as part of what he described as a prolonged investigation.

The crash prompted a massive emergency response, with firefighters, police officers and rescue ambulances converging on the intersection during the evening commute.

Several tents and vendor setups were damaged by the debris strewn around the area, including one of the subway's shelters.

Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass confirmed that street vendors and pedestrians were among those struck.

"I'm heartbroken for the families of everyone impacted," Bass said in a statement posted to social media .

The mayor said her office was coordinating with city departments and emergency responders as authorities worked to determine the cause of the collision.

The victims' identities and ages have not been released, and police have not disclosed the driver's identity.

It remains unclear whether the driver suffered a medical emergency before the crash or whether any criminal charges will be filed.

Authorities closed portions of Lankershim and Chandler boulevards as investigators examined the scene.

articles.title: Coded calls from Brooklyn jail: How Iran-backed operative coordinated terror plots in Europe, US
articles.summary: A suspected Iran-backed terror plot targeting a British airbase used by the US military was allegedly being coordinated, in part, from a New York prison,
articles.body: A suspected Iran-backed terror plot targeting a British airbase used by the US military was allegedly being coordinated, in part, from a New York prison, where an accused operative used coded messages to communicate with associates, according to an indictment unsealed on Tuesday.The accused, Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi, a dual Iranian-Iraqi national, allegedly used calls with his mother and sister to relay instructions to operatives outside prison.US prosecutors claim the messages were intended to keep plans for an attack on RAF Fairford in western England alive.The indictment, reported by the Associated Press, provides fresh details about the suspected plot that came to light on September 27, when three suspicious vans were spotted heading towards the air base. Several men were subsequently detained on suspicion of explosives and terrorism offences.Al-Saadi was already behind bars at New York's Metropolitan Detention Center in Brooklyn when the alleged communications took place. He had been arrested in the spring.Prosecutors have also charged two alleged associates, Iranian national Mohsen Mohajeri and Iraqi national Mohammad Ali al-Hassani. They accuse the three of working with Iran-backed operatives to plan nearly 20 attacks against Jewish communities in Europe and the US. Neither Mohajeri nor al-Hassani is in American custody.US alleges Iran-backed network plotted multiple attacksManhattan US attorney Jamie McDonald said the accused were involved in planning attacks on Jewish communities as well as the British base, which houses American military personnel.“These defendants helped orchestrate a campaign of terror on behalf of terrorist organizations affiliated with Iran that targeted Jewish communities in Europe and the United States, and the British military base, RAF Fairford, housing American service members,” McDonald said."The threat presented by Iran and Iran-backed terrorist groups to America and our allies is not hypothetical - it is very real.”Attorney General Todd Blanche warned that those targeting American military installations would face prosecution.“Anyone who plans a terrorist plot on a military base housing American service members will be prosecuted by the United States government.”The suspected Fairford plot had triggered a security response in Britain. Seven men arrested in connection with the incident were initially released on bail. Two were later arrested again on suspicion of assisting Iran's intelligence service and charged under Britain's National Security Act.Tehran denied involvement after British authorities linked the incident to Iran. The US subsequently pulled its bombers out of RAF Fairford and sent them back to the United States.The base, located around 160 kilometres west of London, has been used by American bombers during several military operations in the Middle East.How prison calls became a channel for instructionsDespite being in custody, al-Saadi allegedly remained in contact with associates through monitored calls with his family. Prosecutors said he used the word “work” as a code for terrorist activity and asked his mother and sister to pass messages to Mohajeri.During a July 30 conversation, he asked his sister: “What are they doing about all our old work?”He wanted to know whether the planned activities had been abandoned or merely suspended. His sister allegedly assured him that “it isn’t cancelled," according to the indictment.In another conversation on September 24, al-Saadi asked about al-Hassani, who had reportedly been moved to the “International Section”. He then told his family to “give him money so we can do it,” prosecutors alleged.Al-Saadi has been held in solitary confinement since his May arrest. The Justice Department has described him as dangerous, citing his alleged willingness to target American and Israeli interests.FBI monitored calls amid concerns over coded languageThe alleged communications have also become part of a legal dispute over al-Saadi's access to his family.Although he was permitted to make phone and video calls from prison, the FBI monitored and recorded the conversations, according to court documents.His lawyer complained in September that several calls had been interrupted or abruptly disconnected. Prosecutors subsequently sought to restrict his access to one hourlong call a month, arguing that he might be using coded expressions such as “work” and “a job” to discuss attacks.Court filings show that al-Saadi made nine phone or video calls between June and September. In one conversation, his mother reportedly cautioned him against discussing a particular subject, saying “they may end the call”. The FBI then terminated the conversation, according to prosecutors.The indictment also details alleged attacks carried out by the network in London. In mid-April, al-Saadi, al-Hassani and Mohajeri allegedly instructed an associate to set fire to a Jewish charity organisation while watching the operation through a video projected from a laptop onto a large screen.A day later, the group allegedly directed another attack on a synagogue in London. Al-Hassani reportedly told the operative to “light it up like a Christmas tree,” the indictment said.Al-Saadi pleaded not guilty in June to allegations that he had plotted at least 18 attacks across Europe in retaliation for the US and Israel's war with Iran. During the proceedings, he described himself as a “prisoner of war”. He has been denied bail and remains in custody.The US has designated both Kata’ib Hizballah and Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps as foreign terrorist organisations. Prosecutors allege that al-Saadi was a commander of Kata’ib Hizballah.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: More debt, less development? Pakistan spends just 10% of annual budget
articles.summary: Pakistan has spent barely 10.4% of its annual development budget in the first four months of the current fiscal year, despite posting a budget surplus in
articles.body: Pakistan has spent barely 10.4% of its annual development budget in the first four months of the current fiscal year, despite posting a budget surplus in the first quarter, raising concerns over delays in public-interest projects and their impact on economic growth and living standards.According to data released by Pakistan's ministry of planning and development, total expenditure under the Public Sector Development Programme (PSDP) between July and October stood at PKR 103.87 billion against an annual allocation of PKR 1 trillion, Dawn reported.Excluding corporations, around 33 ministries and divisions spent just PKR 74.65 billion, or about 11% of their total allocation of PKR 682 billion. Corporations, mainly in the power sector and the national highways authority, spent another PKR 29 billion, amounting to 9.3% of their annual allocation of PKR 313 billion.The slow pace of development spending comes even as Pakistan recorded a budget surplus of 0.8% in the first quarter of the fiscal year.Under the spending mechanism announced by the finance ministry, the Shehbaz Sharif government is expected to release 15% of the annual development allocation in the first quarter, 20% in the second, 25% in the third and the remaining amount in the final quarter. The arrangement is intended to ensure that any shortfall in revenue collection can be managed through cuts in development spending while meeting fiscal targets agreed with the International Monetary Fund (IMF).Meanwhile, Pakistan's dependence on foreign borrowing continues to grow. Its external debt nearly doubled over the past decade, rising from $68.67 billion in 2015 to $135.1 billion in 2025, according to a World Bank report cited by Dawn.The debt stock included $107.07 billion in public and publicly guaranteed loans, $17.58 billion in private non-guaranteed debt and $10.45 billion in short-term borrowing.Multilateral institutions accounted for the largest share of public debt at $56.83 billion, followed by bilateral lenders at $42.43 billion and private creditors at $7.8 billion. China was Pakistan's largest individual creditor, with outstanding loans of $22.4 billion, followed by the World Bank at $19.2 billion and the Asian Development Bank at $16.83 billion.You use AI every day. articles.body: While romantic clichés would suggest feelings don't ask for an invitation, real-life encounters prove love remains unpredictable in its ways. A lifetime together can be traced back to a brushed shoulder on a crowded street or a forgotten handkerchief on a bus seat. For Richard Porritt Sr. and Jean Wadsten, it started abroad, on a train, with a passing glance and little encouragement from friends. What followed outlasted the wartime separation that tested their marriage, preserved in the hundreds of letters exchanged across the Pacific.A train journey across the United States in June 1944, the National WWII Museum records, brought the couple together. Richard, a Navy ensign with orders to report to the USS Tazewell, noticed Jean during a stop in Chicago. She was travelling west with her sister and four-year-old niece. He assumed she was married. By the next terminal, his friends persuaded him to dig further.According to the National WWII Museum, the men flipped a coin to decide who would approach her, and as fate would have it, Richard won the toss. He learnt that Jean was unmarried and that the little girl was her niece, Janet. He and his friends began visiting Jean’s compartment. She enjoyed their company, though Richard became the one she wanted to talk to.Jean grew up in a strict Lutheran upbringing, while Richard, whose parents were divorced, was described as impulsive and less restrained in his speech and behaviour. The differences did not stop either of them from falling in love. When they were able to meet, Richard arranged dates around San Francisco. They ate out, danced and walked in the city’s parks. Before the summer was over, he had decided he wanted to marry Jean. Soon after, he proposed in a cinema, and she accepted. They married in September 1944 and spent their honeymoon in San Francisco, according to the National WWII Museum.However, their time together was rather brief. The USS Tazewell was commissioned and sent from San Francisco to Seattle to take on personnel and supplies. It then sailed for Hawaii, where it embarked garrison troops for the Palau Islands before steaming onward. Richard’s assignment meant that the newlyweds would be separated for a period.Per the museum’s account, the letters began in December 1944. Richard asked Jean to write often: “You see, darling, mail is a fellow’s whole life out here and it’s the greatest morale builder there is.” Richard’s words echoed the sentiment of men serving at sea, for whom letters were the only link to the world they had left behind.Letters of love, family and futureJean sent cards and letters, often using Valentine’s Day as an occasion for a personal message. Her first Valentine that year arrived in January in the form of an illustrated fold-out card. It contained a self-deprecating poem and a short message in her teal ink, “Love, guess who!” An arrow directed Richard to turn the card over for the answer.She wrote about missing him, longing for his return and waiting to feel the baby move. In a letter sent shortly before Christmas, Jean had told him that she suspected she was pregnant. The news delighted Richard even as he regretted being away. Jean also kept him informed about family matters and events at home. Richard, on the other hand, wrote what he could disclose of his service, his efforts to stop gambling, and his intention to read the Bible. He even promised to curb his habit of swearing.In the weeks that followed, Jean sent more cards. One contained a portrait of herself for Richard to keep beside his bed. In another letter, written two days before Valentine’s Day, she recalled their time together before the Navy took him away. She left a lipstick kiss on the final page and sprayed the stationery with the perfume she had worn at their wedding and honeymoon. A month after the holiday, she used an unused Valentine card as a general, crossing out words that no longer fit.Richard kept the cards and correspondence; the museum holds hundreds of their exchanges from December 1944 until November 1945. Their letters also record the future they tried to imagine. For Richard, it was a toss-up between the Navy, teaching or settling near relatives on the North Atlantic coast or in California. He did not want a life that would warrant further separations. For Jean, it was less about the location and more about being together. Both wanted a large family.Their first child was born in August 1945, while Richard was still in the Pacific and serving as a lieutenant junior grade. Eventually, the couple had five children; one died in infancy. They remained married for 64 years. Later, their children donated their letters to the National WWII Museum.You use AI every day. articles.title: Trump claims 'huge victory' as judge allows proceedings in $10 billion defamation lawsuit against BBC
articles.summary: A US federal judge on Tuesday allowed President Donald Trump's $10 billion defamation lawsuit against the BBC to proceed, while denying Trump's unfair
articles.body: A US federal judge on Tuesday allowed President Donald Trump's $10 billion defamation lawsuit against the BBC to proceed, while denying Trump's unfair trade practices claim against the broadcaster.Florida district court judge Jeffrey T Kuntz ruled that Trump had plausibly alleged reputational damage from the BBC's Panorama documentary, Trump: A Second Chance, which spliced together separate remarks he made nearly 55 minutes apart, the Guardian reported.“Accepting the allegations in the complaint as true, the court finds Trump plausibly pled damages where Trump alleges a defamatory documentary released toward the election caused reputational harm,” Kuntz wrote.The judge said the editing could support an inference that the BBC had acted with actual malice, a legal standard that public figures must establish to win defamation cases.“On its face, the editing may independently establish the plausibility of actual malice,” he wrote, rejecting the BBC's argument that the edits were routine measures to condense a 70-minute speech into a 12-second segment.“Editing is often required. However, given the time disparity between the two statements, the distance itself tends toward a plausible inference that BBC knew or should have known that the segment they were creating would not and could not have been a truthful statement. This was not trimming around the edges but creating something different than what was stated in the speech,” Kuntz added.Trump welcomed the ruling on Truth Social, calling it a “huge victory”. “We will continue fighting against, and defeating, all of those who try to deceive the American People!” he said.The judge also referred to previous errors in the BBC's coverage of Trump, saying they could be relevant to assessing whether the broadcaster had acted recklessly. He said Trump's allegations that the BBC had departed from journalistic standards were sufficient to plausibly establish more than negligence.The BBC said it was surprised by the decision but respected the court's authority. “We remain confident in our position and will continue to respond through the proper legal process,” the broadcaster said in a statement.However, according to the Guardian, the ruling does not establish that the BBC is liable for defamation. Trump will still have to prove at trial that the broadcaster acted with actual malice and that he suffered actual damages from the documentary's broadcast. The judge also noted that the programme was not aired in Florida.Kuntz dismissed Trump's claim that the BBC had violated Florida's Deceptive and Unfair Trade Practices Act.You use AI every day. articles.summary: KANPUR:A 15-year-old cloth shop worker was stabbed to death near his home and barely 50 steps from a police outpost in Kanpur’s Fazalganj area late on
articles.body: KANPUR:A 15-year-old cloth shop worker was stabbed to death near his home and barely 50 steps from a police outpost in Kanpur’s Fazalganj area late on Tuesday night. Police have detained one accused and formed five teams to trace the others.Police said the preliminary investigation indicated that a dispute involving a girl could have led to the killing.ACP Jyoti Shri said an FIR has been registered and several police teams are conducting raids to make arrest of the accused possible.Harshit, son of Mahesh Kumar alias Champa, lived in Bamba Road Sabzi Mandi lane in Darshanpurwa.He was walking near his house around 11 on Tuesday night when he allegedly had an argument with Akshat, Raje and Manku, who were sitting by the roadside and consuming liquor.Mahesh alleged that the three boys assaulted Harshit with kicks and punches. When he tried to escape, they chased and caught him before one of them stabbed him in the chest near the heart. The attackers then fled.Harshit reportedly lay injured on the road for about 20 minutes before his family and neighbours took him to Lala Lajpat Rai hospital, where he was declared dead.Residents alleged that neither police personnel nor bystanders intervened despite the crime scene being close to Darshanpurwa outpost and about 25 steps from Harshit’s house.Police personnel from the circle and a forensic team inspected the scene. Liquor bottles and glasses containing liquor were found nearby. Police sources said raids were intensified based on information provided by the detained accused.Mahesh said one accused worked at a lassi shop in Jarib Chowki and alleged that he committed the murder with his associates. articles.title: A California man kept his family’s blanket in a closet for years; experts identified a circa-1840 Navajo First Phase chief’s blanket, which sold for $1.8 million, including fees
articles.summary: A California man discovers that a family heirloom blanket, long considered worthless, is actually a rare 1840 Navajo chief's blanket that sold for $1.8 million at auction. Explore the history and significance of this extraordinary textile artifact.
articles.body: An old blanket kept in a family closet for years turned out to be a valuable piece of Native American textile history. A man in California had inherited the piece and initially thought it was just a family heirloom until it was looked at more closely. John Moran Auctioneers said the blanket was a rare Navajo First Phase chief's blanket from the mid-19th-century period, which it sold at auction for some $1.8 million, including fees.The revelation showed how potentially precious artefacts can sit in an individual's house for years and end up as a badly faded domestic blanket. The blanket was an actual example of early Navajo weaving, an art form with a long tradition known for its skill, design and historical value. Its sale also showed the elite interest in the history of Navajo textiles and collectors' fascination with indigenous work.A family heirloom that remained unnoticed for generationsThe blanket originated with Loren Krytzer, who lived in California and her ancestor, a Norwegian immigrant, John Chantland. It can be traced back to the 1870s, when Chantland, who owned a general store in Mayville, Dakota Territory, traded for it. The textile then stayed in the family for 142 years, handed down from generation to generation until it appeared in a museum.Krytzer kept the blanket in a cupboard for years, oblivious to its historical value, and he had little reason to think that the one old piece of textile would fetch much. That was until 2011, when he saw an episode of the TV program Antiques Roadshow in which an elderly man presented a comparable Navajo blanket, which was valued at $ 500,000.He recognised the similarity and started to re-evaluate the family's piece. He ultimately submitted the item for auction at John Moran Auctioneers in California in March 2012. The auction house determined that it was an exceptionally rare First Phase Navajo chief's blanket from around 1840, with the piece's history with the Chatland family and its pristine condition both contributing to its value.Why the 1840 Navajo blanket was so valuableThe gold blanket was valued for its age, the weaving, the material, and the rarity. The approximate dimensions are 171.5 by 141 cm. It was hand-spun and woven in natural ivory, dark brown and black, and indigo-dyed blue and lac-dyed red fibres. The weaving shows a concentration on horizontal stripes rather than the complex geometrical patterns that were produced in later phases of Navajo weaving. The first phase blanket, which was introduced around 1800, had a reputation for its close weave and symmetrical use of colour, and was worn as a shoulder garment and traded widely to people on the Great Plains.The title chief's blanket is a modern invention, but its status and connection with wealthy wearers suggest the name is applicable. Research published in KIVA looks at the transmission of weaving skills and design among the Navajo kingship groups, which provides some explanation as to why these older weavings are appreciated and collected as a cultural object, not just as find textiles.A record-breaking auction and an unexpected fortune John Moran Auctioneers initially valued the blanket at between $100,000 and $200,000, but collectors and dealers quickly drove the price far higher. Scientific testing on the dye showed that the red contained lac dyes and the blue contained indigo, with no indication of any synthetic dyes, confirming that the blanket was genuine and from 1800. The item was auctioned on 19 June 2012 at a Pasadena Convention Centre in California, and following heated bidding from online and on-site bidders, the winning bid was placed by the dealer based in New York, Donald Ellis, for $ 1.5 million. The item eventually sold for $ 1.8 million.The estimate was far exceeded, setting a new auction record for Navajo textiles and surpassing the previous high of $522,500 set in 1989 for a First Phase chief’s blanket. The sale is a reminder of how historic art can preserve outstanding culture and monetary value, even while the value of the blanket is more than just scale. Thus, the value of the Chantland blanket is more than just a tag at auction. It is a skill of Navajo weavers, a symbol of indigenous textile trading, and the preservation of traditional craftsmanship across generations.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: A Navy veteran’s 1946 letter to his high-school sweetheart was sealed inside an Illinois home’s wall; renovators found it 70 years later and returned it to him at age 90
articles.summary: A remarkable story of love transcending time as a 1946 letter from a Navy veteran to his high school sweetheart is discovered in a wall of an Illinois home and returned to him 70 years later.
articles.body: The letter was written by a young US Navy sailor to his high school sweetheart in April 1946. It was found inside the wall of a home in Illinois several decades later. When the letter was discovered and returned to the 90-year-old sailor in October 2016, a tender reunion between a man and his long-lost love took place. Lt. McCabe, the man who penned the words in the letter, addressed it to a young woman named Juanita Gibbs.A wartime letter hidden inside a homeTom Moore and his wife, Laura, found the letter during the renovation of an old house in Quincy, Illinois, where it had been buried in loose packing paper removed from a wall. They found the correspondence with the name on it, ‘ Lt. Kenneth L. McCabe,’ and the intended recipient, Juanita Gibbs. It was dated April 1946, placing it after the Second World War had ended. By the time he wrote it, the Navy vet was assisting in Guam, having spent about a year and a half in the service, including in the South Pacific.Apparently, neither of them received the letter, or they did but never opened it, so it was stored away in the building. What that letter gave us, in any case, was a peek at a relationship that had started well before he had even penned that letter. According to the Navy Times, McCabe described that she was the girl he dated in high school and fell in love with before he got down on one knee and married her on October 25, 1947. They had three kids, and they were together until she passed away.Renovators trace the letter’s original writer Instead of treating the old letter as a mundane object to be thrown away, he decided to try to track down the person the letter was addressed to. Moore started ringing around and searching for McCabe to see if he could determine whether he was alive and to try to get in touch with him. He sought advice from a friend, who told him to look into a local Honor Flight group. Honor Flight is a not-for-profit organisation that arranges trips to national memorials for eligible military personnel, with a particular focus on those who served in the Second World War and subsequent conflicts.The resolution to search brought a simple home renovation to a joyful conclusion. Moore was able to place the letter in McCabe's hands at his work. Marine Corps Times reported that the other workers gathered around the man as he accepted the historic letter and applauded him as he was able to reconnect to the lifetime period it documented. It was especially poignant to reestablish the relationship since Juanita wasn't around to get the letter.A personal reminder of wartime relationshipMcCabe was amazed that the letter was still intact. “When I think back to Juanita, I just remember the good wife and mother she was,” he said, adding that he appreciated the effort Moore went into returning the correspondence instead of throwing it away. “I am really looking forward to getting back home and sitting down and reading what I wrote all those years ago, because it wasn't just the one letter I wrote.” The note from McCabe adds weight to the significance of personal letters, especially those retained during lengthy military separation.Sending a letter home was a vital part of communication between servicemen and those left behind. Personal notes can preserve everyday emotions and intimate concerns that official accounts do not tend to reveal. For McCabe, this letter wasn't just a piece from the past; it was a bridge back to his youth, to the Navy, and to the woman he considered his first love.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'Even if pollution increased on Diwali, it would eventually subside': UP CM Yogi
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Wednesday defended Diwali celebrations involving firecrackers amid concerns over worsening air
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Wednesday defended Diwali celebrations involving firecrackers amid concerns over worsening air pollution. The Uttar Pradesh CM said that even if pollution levels increased during the festival, they would eventually subside.Addressing an event, Adityanath questioned why pollution became a major concern when people celebrated festivals, while those responsible for allegedly corrupting the system were not held accountable. He also defended the use of firecrackers, saying his government had not imposed restrictions on them during Diwali."You celebrated Diwali as well, but many people complained that it caused pollution. I said that even if pollution increased, it would eventually subside, so why worry?" the chief minister said."Nobody questions those who polluted the entire system through their corrupt practices. But if the public celebrates Diwali with firecrackers for just one day, suddenly it becomes a major pollution issue. Even if pollution occurs, it will eventually settle down. That is not a major concern," he added.Adityanath further said people had done the right thing by celebrating Diwali enthusiastically and bursting firecrackers. "People did the right thing by celebrating Diwali with great enthusiasm and bursting plenty of firecrackers. We had also said that there would be no restrictions on firecrackers," he said.His remarks come amid a sharp deterioration in air quality across north India following Diwali celebrations. Delhi recorded its most polluted Diwali in five years, with an average Air Quality Index (AQI) of 376 on Sunday.Lucknow recorded an AQI of 245, while Varanasi stood at 274 and Gorakhpur at 261, as per a report by PTI.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: After affair revelation, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang held regular meetings at the company's headquarters, apologised again, and quickly moved to 'business as usual'
articles.summary: Days after admitting his affair with Alice Huang, former CEO of Singapore-based Megaspeed, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang walked into the chipmaker’s Santa
articles.body: Days after admitting his affair with Alice Huang, former CEO of Singapore-based Megaspeed, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang walked into the chipmaker’s Santa Clara, California, headquarters. According to a CNBC report, the Nvidia Chief conducted closed-door meetings with top-level executives where he addressed his infidelity. Stating how sorry he was to his staff, Jensen Huang didn’t take any questions and quickly moved to business and top agenda items of the day, sources familiar with the matter told the publication. Jensen Huang admitted to his affair on November 8 in a company-wide email to employees without disclosing with whom he had the relationship.“I know an apology cannot undo what I have done,” he wrote in the email. “I hope our family will heal and that, over time, I can earn back your trust,” Huang added.Jensen Huang gets down to business as usual at Nvidia after ‘spy scandal’As stated in the CNBC report, people inside the chip giant said Jensen Huang tried to project “business as usual,” even as the probe moved forward into his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Nvidia employees described the mood to CNBC as “sad” after the revelation. The report quotes an employee who said that they were shocked by Jensen Huang’s revelations.Meanwhile, Nvidia’s board opened an independent investigation and hired Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct the probe. In a fresh statement, the NVIDIA board said “The independent members of the NVIDIA Board have retained former acting U.S. Attorney of the Southern District of New York Joon H. Kim and his firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct a thorough and independent investigation as was announced on Sunday.”Jensen Huang CCed his kids in emailNotably, Jensen Huang’s apology email to employees over his marital infidelity also contained a direct appeal to his family, including his two children who work at the AI chipmaker. The email, released by Nvidia on November 8, opened with Jensen Huang saying: “I owe my family and all of you an apology.” He then wrote: “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”The message included a section addressed specifically to his wife and family. “To my wife and family: I love you. I know an apology cannot undo what I have done. I hope our family will heal and that, over time, I can earn back your trust,” Huang wrote.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Advantage China? How Nvidia CEO's affair with 'spy' Alice Huang could impact US
articles.summary: Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang's admission of an extramarital affair has triggered a political and national security storm in Washington, with
articles.body: Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang's admission of an extramarital affair has triggered a political and national security storm in Washington, with questions emerging over whether his relationship with a Chinese businesswoman suspected of espionage could have exposed sensitive American technology to Beijing. What might have remained a private matter has now become a major concern for US lawmakers, intelligence officials and the world's most valuable artificial intelligence (AI) chipmaker.The woman at the centre of the controversy, Alice Huang, is a former executive at Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed, which has faced allegations of helping route advanced Nvidia chips to Chinese buyers in violation of US export restrictions. US intelligence officials have reportedly concluded that she spied for China, although Beijing has rejected the allegations as unsubstantiated. The US Department of Justice (DoJ) has opened an investigation into Megaspeed's activities, while Nvidia's board has launched an independent review of its chief executive's interactions with the businesswoman.The controversy comes at a particularly sensitive time for Washington, which has made maintaining its lead over China in AI a major economic and national security priority. With Nvidia supplying the vast majority of high-end chips powering American AI development, any compromise involving the company could have consequences extending well beyond its leadership, potentially affecting US-China relations, technology exports and the broader AI industry.Why Nvidia is central to America's AI ambitionsNvidia has become one of the most important companies in the global technology industry, with its graphics processing units (GPUs) forming the backbone of modern AI systems and data centres. Originally developed primarily for video gaming, these chips have proved particularly effective at the complex calculations required to train and operate advanced AI models.The company is estimated to control more than 80% of the high-end AI chip market, making it difficult for American technology companies to develop advanced AI systems without relying on its products.This dominance has also made Nvidia central to Washington's efforts to restrict China's access to advanced semiconductor technology. The US has imposed export controls on powerful Nvidia chips since 2022, seeking to slow Beijing's progress in developing sophisticated AI systems that could have military and cybersecurity applications.However, Huang has repeatedly argued that Nvidia should be allowed to sell some less advanced chips, including its H200 processors, to Chinese companies. He believes restricting access could push Chinese businesses towards domestic chipmakers, eventually weakening America's influence over the global AI ecosystem.Megaspeed has previously faced allegations of purchasing advanced Nvidia chips and routing them to Chinese customers. Trade records cited in reports indicate that more than $3 billion worth of chips moved from Singapore to China in a single year, alongside substantial shipments from Malaysia. Espionage fears and political scrutiny growThe immediate concern for American intelligence officials is what information China may have obtained through Alice Huang's alleged connections with Nvidia's chief executive.According to Politico, officials fear Beijing could have gained access to privileged information about Nvidia's chip technology, manufacturing capabilities and future business plans. Such information could help Chinese companies narrow the technological gap with American competitors.Retired General Leslie Beavers, a former Pentagon intelligence official, told Politico that Washington should be particularly concerned about China gaining insights into how advanced chips are manufactured and how their performance and reliability are achieved.Glenn Gerstell, former general counsel for the National Security Agency, warned that the alleged incident highlighted how China's intelligence network could reach into Silicon Valley. He said the private sector was "every bit as important to our national security as the government is".The controversy has also prompted calls for congressional scrutiny. Republican leaders of the House Foreign Affairs, Intelligence and China committees have sought a closed-door briefing with Huang, while Democratic lawmakers have demanded answers about Nvidia's safeguards against foreign espionage.Ro Khanna, ranking member of the House China Committee, called for a classified briefing, saying lawmakers needed to understand the national security risks before deciding on further action.Trump's ties with Huang complicate US responseThe scandal also puts President Donald Trump in a difficult position, given his close relationship with Huang and Nvidia's importance to his economic agenda.Trump has repeatedly praised the Nvidia chief, viewing the company as central to his ambition of making the US the global leader in AI. The two have maintained regular contact since their first dinner at Mar-a-Lago in early 2025. Huang also accompanied Trump on Air Force One during a state visit to Beijing earlier this year.Trump defended the executive after the controversy emerged, saying he had spoken to him and believed he had no knowledge that Alice Huang was allegedly a spy. "I think he’ll be in good shape," the president said.However, any action against Nvidia could carry significant economic consequences. The company's growth has been closely tied to the AI investment boom, which has also driven gains across the US stock market. Nvidia is a key supplier and investor within an interconnected technology ecosystem involving AI developers, chipmakers and data centre operators.According to Politico, US officials face a difficult choice: failing to address a potential espionage breach could compromise national security, but imposing restrictions on Nvidia could weaken America's own AI industry and potentially benefit Chinese competitors.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'Gave up PM post, became Super PM': BJP targets Sonia Gandhi over UPA role after memoir release
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: BJP Rajya Sabha member Sudhanshu Trivedi on Wednesday criticised senior Congress leader Sonia Gandhi over her role during the UPA government,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: BJP Rajya Sabha member Sudhanshu Trivedi on Wednesday criticised senior Congress leader Sonia Gandhi over her role during the UPA government, claiming she gave up the Prime Minister's post in 2004 but went on to become a “Super PM” as chairperson of the National Advisory Council (NAC).Addressing a presser, Trivedi questioned how Sonia could decline the Prime Minister's office while holding a Cabinet minister-ranked position in the NAC, alleging that she continued to wield considerable influence over the Manmohan Singh government.“She gave up the post of Prime Minister and became a Super PM. You will not find such an example anywhere in the world, where someone gives up the post of Prime Minister but takes the rank of a Cabinet minister,” Trivedi said.He also questioned Sonia's appointment as NAC chairperson, claiming the position carried the rank of a Cabinet minister and came under the Office of Profit provisions.“She became the chairperson of the National Advisory Council (NAC), with the rank of a Cabinet minister, and that too under the Office of Profit,” he said.“I believe all these facts are before the people of the country, and everyone knows what the Super PM and Super Cabinet were during that period of governance,” Trivedi added.His remarks come amid the political debate surrounding Sonia's memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, released on Tuesday. In the book, former Congress chief recounts the circumstances that led her to decline the Prime Minister's post after the Congress-led alliance won the 2004 Lok Sabha elections.Sonia writes that she had initially ruled out becoming Prime Minister during a conversation with her children, Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra. Both had opposed her taking the position, having experienced the trauma of the assassinations of their grandmother, former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, and their father, Rajiv Gandhi.She recalls that alliance leaders subsequently pressed her to accept the post, prompting her to reluctantly say “theek hai”. However, after reflecting on the decision, she told Rahul Gandhi that she would stick to her original stand.Sonia later announced in Parliament that she would follow her “inner voice” and nominated Manmohan Singh as the Congress parliamentary party leader, paving the way for him to become Prime Minister.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Babar premis will be punished': BJP targets TMC's Kirti Azad over Ram Mandir remarks
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari on Wednesday criticised Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP Kirti Azad over his remarks on Lord Ram and the Ayodhya
articles.body: NEW DELHI: BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari on Wednesday criticised Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP Kirti Azad over his remarks on Lord Ram and the Ayodhya Ram Mandir, accusing the opposition of engaging in “peak vote bank politics”.In a post on X, Bhandari accused the TMC of insulting Lord Ram and alleged that the Congress-led INDIA bloc was opposed to Sanatan.“Congress lead Opposition hates Sanatan! TMC MP insults Prabhu Shree Ram! By asking their leaders to continue to slander Sanatan Rahul Gandhi, Mamta Banerjee and Akhilesh Yadav are practising 'Peak vote bank politics'.He also warned that opposition parties would face punishment in the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, similar to the TMC's electoral defeat in West Bengal.“Babar Premis will be punished by people of Uttar Pradesh just like Bengal,” Bhandari wrote.The BJP leader's remarks came after Azad said he would never visit the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya, questioning the treatment of Maa Sita by Lord Ram.Speaking to news agency ANI, the TMC MP said he did not consider Lord Ram the only deity worthy of worship and referred to Maa Sita as his mother, saying he belonged to her birthplace, Mithila.“Is Lord Ram the only God among the 3,200 crore deities in our country? I will never go there because Lord Ram abandoned his wife, even after she had passed the Agni Pariksha and sent Maa Sita away from his home,” he said.“Why should I go? I belong to the birthplace of Maa Sita. She was the daughter of Mithila. Maa Sita is my mother. For every person belonging to Mithila, Maa Sita is a mother,” he added.Azad questioned the description of Lord Ram as “Maryada Purushottam” and said he worshipped Maa Kali. He also named temples he visits, including Kamakhya, Dakshina Kali, Kalighat and the Kali Temple at Gol Market in Delhi.“Does that mean I am not a Hindu?” he asked.The row erupted ahead of Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav's proposed visit to the Ram Mandir in December, ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: INS Betwa set for major propulsion upgrade under Rs 498 crore deal
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The ministry of defence on Wednesday signed a Rs 498.58 crore contract with Cochin Shipyard Limited for the refit and re-powering of Indian
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The ministry of defence on Wednesday signed a Rs 498.58 crore contract with Cochin Shipyard Limited for the refit and re-powering of Indian Navy warship INS Betwa.Under the agreement, the Brahmaputra-class frigate will undergo a major transformation, with its existing steam-based propulsion system being replaced by a diesel-engine-based system. The refit will also involve upgrading the warship's combat capabilities through the installation of a modernised weapons suite, aimed at improving its operational effectiveness.The project is expected to strengthen India's indigenous ship repair and maintenance capabilities, particularly in carrying out complex propulsion system upgrades and modernisation of naval platforms. More than 50 micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) are expected to be involved in the project, which is also likely to generate employment opportunities across the country's shipbuilding and ancillary industries.The ministry said the initiative would provide a boost to the government's vision of ‘Aatmanirbhar Bharat’ and ‘Make in India’, while reinforcing domestic capabilities in naval ship maintenance and modernisation.INS Betwa, the second indigenously built Brahmaputra-class guided missile frigate, was commissioned into the Indian Navy on July 7, 2004. The 3,600-tonne warship measures 125 metres in length and is capable of speeds exceeding 30 knots. It is manned by 40 officers and 330 sailors.The vessel is equipped with a range of guns, surface-to-surface and surface-to-air missiles, torpedo launchers and maritime surveillance sensors.

articles.title: 'Acid balloon' memories are back for Microsoft in Amsterdam, what's bringing the 'nightmare' back for software giant
articles.summary: A group of protesters recently stormed the construction site of a massive Microsoft data center on the outskirts of Amsterdam, marking the second incident
articles.body: A group of protesters recently stormed the construction site of a massive Microsoft data center on the outskirts of Amsterdam, marking the second incident in one year where the tech giant’s AI infrastructure site has been attacked. The latest security breach follows earlier hostility at the same site, bringing back unwelcome memories for the software giant wherein activists targeted the exact same location with acid-filled balloons. The incident also marked a sharp escalation in European demonstrations against large-scale tech infrastructure. Riot police were deployed to the scene near Sloterdijk, in Amsterdam’s western port area, and made multiple arrests.How the attack on Microsoft unfoldedAccording to Dutch news agency ANP, police initially blocked the demonstration march. After Amsterdam’s mayor issued an order banning the gathering, marchers attempted to push past police lines before heading toward the construction grounds, where work is underway on a major three-building complex intended for Microsoft.Reports from local media said that roughly 100 people breached the site’s boundaries, while around 500 demonstrators entered the grounds, some remaining outside. Local news portal AN5 reported that several protesters cut or broke through perimeter fences to get in, while others climbed an on-site construction crane.Previously, the protestors filled water balloons with a mixture of hydrogen peroxide, acetic acid, salt and acrylic paint before throwing them at the facility, according to the Register.“This acidic mixture attacks concrete, and the hydrogen peroxide causes steel to rust faster,” said the group in a statement at that time. Activists have also spattered the offices of fossil fuel insurers with foul-smelling butyric acid and used superglue and bicycle locks to barricade the entrance of Lloyd's, a major insurance market in London.Why protesters are targeting the data centerGeef Tegengas, an advocacy group that campaigns against fossil fuels, is demanding an immediate and permanent halt to the project, arguing that it puts too much strain on local power grids. The group claims the completed facility will consume as much electricity as every household in Amsterdam combined. They warn that the massive power draw will derail the construction of 30,000 planned local homes.The development consists of three separate 85-meter-tall towers, all of which will be leased entirely by Microsoft. Initial plans for the complex were submitted in 2016—before Amsterdam enacted a municipal ban on new data center builds within the city.Meanwhile, the event’s organisers slammed the police response. “They behaved disgracefully,” they claimed. “There is a right to demonstrate in this country, and that is being completely disregarded; even the march to the data center was not facilitated.”You use AI every day. articles.body: Russia struck six large electricity substations across four central regions of Ukraine, Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi said on Wednesday, as the second day of peace talks between Ukraine, Russia and the United States began in Abu Dhabi.Koretskyi said Russian forces had also targeted railway infrastructure in eastern and central Ukraine, in addition to the attacks on energy facilities.In a post on Telegram, the Ukrainian prime minister said six major electricity substations had been hit, but did not immediately provide details of the damage.Meanwhile, the second day of trilateral peace talks between Ukraine, Russia and the United States began in Abu Dhabi on Wednesday, Kyiv's chief negotiator confirmed to news agency Reuters.Earlier, Ukrainian news outlet Ukrainska Pravda reported that Russian forces had attacked energy infrastructure in the Ternopil, Kirovohrad, Rivne, Volyn, Odesa and Zhytomyr regions on the evening of November 3 and overnight into November 4.You use AI every day. articles.title: New York is testing a road surface made with the equivalent of 1.9 million plastic bottles and 96% recycled material; this unique asphalt mix could reduce emissions and make city roads more durable
articles.summary: In an attempt to lower construction emissions and increase the longevity of its streets, New York City is testing a novel road surface made from recycled
articles.body: In an attempt to lower construction emissions and increase the longevity of its streets, New York City is testing a novel road surface made from recycled plastic bottles and industrial waste. The equivalent of over 1.9 million plastic bottles are incorporated into one of the experimental asphalt mixtures, while another contains 96% recycled material. The Bronx trials, on Fordham Road, could provide a new method of recycling rejected materials and help the city address its persistent road maintenance problems. The project also offers an opportunity to test the durability of recycled materials in the face of the demands of busy urban traffic.New York's recycled asphalt could reduce emissions and improve road durabilityThe New York City Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is testing two new asphalt mixes aimed at making road construction more sustainable. Its October 23, 2026 announcement said the materials use recycled plastic and steel production waste to reduce conventional ingredients.The first mixture incorporates steel slag, a byproduct generated during steel manufacturing. The second uses recycled plastic, including material derived from drinking bottles, to modify the asphalt binder instead of relying on virgin polymers.The initiative is part of a broader push to find practical uses for waste materials in infrastructure. Instead of sending industrial waste and discarded plastic to landfill, the city is investigating if they could be useful ingredients for road surfaces.As explained by CTA Architects, the trials demonstrate how construction materials can be reused within a circular system, reducing waste while potentially lowering the environmental impact of infrastructure projects.What makes the two experimental asphalt mixtures differentThe steel slag mixture contains 96% recycled material, including 66% recycled steel slag aggregate. Steel slag is left behind during steel production and is being tested as a replacement for conventional aggregate in the road surface.NYC DOT says incorporating steel slag into asphalt could reduce greenhouse gas emissions while improving pavement durability. This could be particularly useful on heavily travelled roads, where surfaces experience repeated pressure from buses, trucks and other vehicles.The plastic-based mixture follows a different approach. Instead of using newly manufactured polymers to modify the asphalt binder, it incorporates recycled plastic. The material includes the equivalent of more than 1.9 million plastic bottles, according to the transportation department.The two approaches are being evaluated separately, allowing the city to examine how different recycled ingredients perform under real road conditions.How much carbon could the plastic asphalt saveThe environmental benefits of the plastic-based asphalt extend beyond recycling bottles. NYC DOT estimates that the material used in this project will prevent approximately 56.6 metric tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent emissions compared with conventional materials.The department says this reduction is comparable to the emissions produced by an average petrol-powered passenger vehicle travelling 144,135 miles. The figure highlights how changes in road construction materials could contribute to lowering emissions, even without altering the basic purpose of the infrastructure.The approach is particularly relevant for cities that regularly need large quantities of asphalt for street repairs and resurfacing.Existing recycled asphalt provides a starting pointNew York is not beginning its recycled asphalt experiments from scratch. NYC DOT already produces asphalt containing an average of 40% recycled material at its two municipal asphalt plants.According to the department, using recycled ingredients helps reduce the amount of new material required for repaving. It can also lower costs associated with transporting discarded materials to landfills.The city has been experimenting with asphalt containing up to 50% recycled roadway materials on a limited scale since 2019, monitoring how the mixtures perform after installation. In 2026, NYC DOT also developed a 50% recycled asphalt pavement mix in-house for future use on city streets.These earlier efforts provide a foundation for the latest experiments, which introduce additional recycled materials beyond those commonly used in existing pavement mixtures.Fordham Road offers a real-world test for the new materialsThe experimental asphalt has been installed on the eastern section of Fordham Road in the Bronx, between Webster Avenue and Southern Boulevard.The location is significant because Fordham Road is undergoing a major redesign intended to improve bus service and street safety. The corridor is part of a project that will introduce offset bus lanes, helping improve bus speed and reliability for approximately 130,000 daily riders.NYC DOT Commissioner Mike Flynn said the department wanted to test the new mixtures as part of the broader transportation improvements while examining how they withstand New York City's challenging weather conditions.The department will monitor the pavement's performance under everyday traffic and changing weather, including the conditions that can place considerable pressure on urban roads.CTA Architects reported that the results could help determine whether these recycled construction materials can be used more widely across the city.The Fordham Road project is part of Mayor Mamdani's Next Stop: Fast Buses, Better Service plan, which aims to make bus journeys faster, more comfortable and reliable. NYC DOT expects the plan to reduce average commuting times by up to six minutes across 175 bus routes.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
